newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER SHOWCASE-LISBON CLASH A TEST OF TWO CITIES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-LISBON CLASH A TEST OF TWO CITIES.

text.p: When reigning champions Porto and their main challengers Benfica meet in Lisbon's Stadium of Light on Saturday, there is far more than soccer at stake.
The eternal rivals carry on their shoulders the pride of Portugal's two leading cities -- Lisbon and Oporto -- and are symbols of the country's north-south regional divide.
Lisbon is the colourful, cultural capital, while Oporto is the country's gritty, industrial motor.

The two sides, both past European Cup winners, have dominated the Portuguese league over the past two decades, winning between them 18 championships and all but eclipsing Sporting, Lisbon's other major club, who have not won the title for 15 years.
Saturday's showdown once again sees them occupying the top two slots in the league, with Porto five points clear of Benfica with 38 points and no other challengers in sight.
Victory for the northern club could effectively wrap up the championship and give them a record third successive title.
The last time Porto travelled to Benfica, last year's Portuguese cup winners, they gave them one of their worst drubbings ever, a 5-0 mauling in September in the Super Cup.
"That defeat belongs to the past. Benfica have grown and we certainly are not going to repeat the same errors," said veteran Belgian goalkeeper Michel Preud'homme.
Since then, Benfica have beefed up their attack by buying Swedish international striker Martin Pringle to partner leading goalscorer Brazilian Osmar Donizete.
The history of league clashes between the two suggests things will be far closer this time.
In the past 10 seasons, half of the games have ended in draws. Of the rest, Benfica have won six and Porto four.
Last year Benfica had the satisfaction of ending an unbeaten Porto run of 53 games, inflicting a 2-1 defeat on the eventual champions who were then coached by former England manager Bobby Robson.

Robson has sinced moved to the bright lights of Spain's Barcelona but his successor Antonio Oliveira, former Portuguese national squad trainer, has succeeded in putting together an equally impressive string of results.
Porto, who are through to the quarter-finals of the European Cup, are unbeaten so far this season in any competition.
